focus.entry: Navigation mode: one tab stop, focus on a cell. Edit mode: DOM focus is in the editor inside the cell.
focus.exit: Enter, Tab, F2 commit; Escape cancels; focus moving outside the cell commits (or cancels, by configuration).
focus.restore: To the edited cell, or to the neighbour named by the committing key.
focus.note: Two modes with different key maps; the engine exposes the mode as state. A rejected commit keeps edit mode open, marks the editor invalid and announces the message.

rtlDecisions.question: Does the engine remap ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End while a text input inside a composite (combobox, tag input, grid cell editor, spinbutton) has focus?
rtlDecisions.apg: The combobox page says Left and Right Arrow move the input cursor one character and warns that scripts must not interfere with browser-provided text editing keys.

libraries.behaviour: The composite returns to native textbox behaviour unless the caret is at the edge it is leaving by and the selection is collapsed.
Autocomplete lets the browser move the caret; it acts on ArrowLeft only when the caret is at index 0 with nothing selected.

rtlDecisions.reason: Caret movement in bidirectional text is the platform's job (visual or logical by OS) and users expect it unchanged. The engine never swaps these keys inside a text input; it only decides when a key leaves the input (see input-edge-handoff).

data.notes: Navigation-mode cell movement is the grid file, including its mirrored horizontal arrows. RTL in edit mode: the arrows are the caret's and are not remapped (decision text-caret). MUI X records the focus target after Tab as "right" and after Shift+Tab as "left"; we state it logically: Tab commits and goes to the next cell in row order, which is the cell to the left in RTL. Numeric and currency editors accept Arabic-Indic digits; a cell holding a number or Latin text inside an RTL grid needs its own direction (dir="auto" or isolation), which also determines which side the caret starts on.
